claims.text: Atomic layer deposition can provide a thin, conformal Ni coating on tungsten particles before spark-plasma sintering.
A Ni coating on W particles will improve Cu infiltration during spark-plasma sintering.
A Ni coating on W particles will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding.
The Ni layer improves W–Cu wettability by reducing the surface-energy mismatch at the interface.
Improved wettability enables near-perfect W–Cu contact during rapid sintering.
The Ni coating enhances interfacial adhesion between W and Cu.
The Ni coating enhances capillary infiltration of molten Cu during sintering.
Enhanced adhesion and Cu infiltration reduce void nucleation and phase separation.
Ni-coated W composites will have a more uniform microstructure and fewer voids than composites made from vapor-coated W powders.
Improved W–Cu interfacial quality will improve thermal transport.
Ni-coated W composites will have higher thermal conductivity than the vapor-coated baseline.
Ni-coated W composites will maintain mechanical strength and durability under simulated fusion-relevant irradiation.
Conventionally vapor-coated and sintered W–Cu material displays incomplete wetting, void formation, and phase separation.
Vapor-coated W powders can be sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between W and Cu, although the resulting material may still contain voids and phase separation.
The Ni-interlayer intervention is expected to remain effective within temperatures and microstructural regimes typical of spark-plasma sintering.

contradictions.description: The vapor-coated baseline is characterized both as having incomplete wetting and as achieving near-perfect constituent contact. Although localized voids could coexist with generally good contact, the stated baseline descriptions are in tension and are not reconciled.
